config.goal: Port adam.cu (HeCBench adam-cuda; grid-stride Adam optimizer, 10 updates per parameter) to idiomatic SYCL 2020 with zero dpct helpers; the float32 parameters must match the C++ reference within atol 1e-5 + rtol 1e-4. Tolerance: 1 - 0.999^t cancels, so a 1-ulp difference in pow (GPU vs CPU libm) becomes a ~6e-5 relative difference in the bias-corrected v. Where v starts near 0 the update m/sqrt(v) is large and p moves by up to ~3 (min p is -2.02), so the error scales with |p|: simulating a 1-ulp pow change gives 3.15e-5 at that element and 8.5e-7 at the 99.99th percentile. The bound is then 6.7x above the worst case and over 10x above the rest, while an indexing, mode or update-order bug moves p by 1e-3 or more.

input.summary: Ported adam.cu to idiomatic SYCL 2020 in migrated/adam.dp.cpp. The file has no dpct includes, helpers, or DPCT_* macros (grep confirmed), and it compiles with icpx -fsycl and add_dpct_include=false with 0 warnings. The kernel is a 1-D nd_range parallel_for with a grid-stride loop, using USM device allocations, sycl::pow/sqrt, and the same update order as the CUDA kernel. Numerical check against the CPU reference (reference.h, same input, 1048576 elements, 10 steps): max abs diff 4.8e-7, all elements within atol 1e-5 + rtol 1e-4; min p = -2.0208. Caveats: no GPU is present on this machine, so the binary runs on the default selector (CPU/OpenCL fallback), and the kernel timing (224 ms) is not representative of GPU performance. The gpu_selector_v choice from the first draft was replaced with default_selector_v for this reason.
